title: Public key infrastructure (PKI) and certificate authorities

videos.script: Every lesson so far has ended on the same open question. Whose public key is this? {{title}} A browser meeting Vereda's portal for the first time receives a public key. It cannot ask the portal whether the key is genuine, because an impostor would say yes. {{question}} The answer is a third party both sides already trust. A certificate authority checks who controls a name, then signs a statement: this key belongs to portal.vereda.example. {{certificate}} The authorities themselves form a hierarchy. A root, kept offline, signs an issuing CA, which signs the server. {{chain}} Your computer ships with a list of roots it trusts. That list decides everything. {{store}} And when a CA gets it wrong, as several have, the whole system has to notice. {{failures}}
